phases.goal: Start where they are strongest — their own project — to get a truthful baseline, not a rehearsed pitch.
phases.probe: “Walk me through the project you're proudest of. What exactly was yours?”
phases.listenFor: Ownership language (“I decided” vs “we were told”); specifics over buzzwords.

phases.goal: Move from what they built to WHY it works — the difference between understanding and recall.
phases.probe: “Why X over Y? What breaks first if we remove Z?”
phases.listenFor: Causal reasoning about their own choices; honest “I don't know” over confabulation.

phases.goal: Change one constraint and watch whether the knowledge generalises or was memorised.
phases.probe: “Same system, but the data is 100× bigger — what changes first?”
phases.listenFor: Re-decomposition under the new constraint, not a recited pattern.

phases.goal: Deliberately offer a hint or gentle pushback mid-problem — the one signal no take-home can capture.
phases.probe: “Have you considered the case where the input arrives out of order?”
phases.listenFor: Hint uptake: integrate and build on it (5) vs acknowledge and ignore (2). Score the uptake, not the answer.

phases.goal: Surface the learning loop — how they behave when nothing works is the best ramp-up predictor we have.
phases.probe: “Where did you get hardest stuck? Walk me through getting out.”
phases.listenFor: A repeatable diagnose–experiment–adjust loop; reflection on what they'd do differently.

phases.goal: Test self-awareness: have them rate themselves, then probe the rating; close on where they want to go.
phases.probe: “Rate your SQL 1–10. What would someone one point above you know that you don't?”
phases.listenFor: Calibrated self-assessment (knowing the shape of what they don't know); intrinsic, specific direction.
